data.name: Mars: War Logs
data.detailed_description:
An Intense Cyberpunk Rpg On the Red Planet!

Mars War Logs takes you to Mars, nearly a century after the cataclysm that threw the planet and its colonists into chaos. Water has become the most precious resource on the arid red planet, with a few companies fighting a perpetual war for its control.


In the middle of this struggle, play as Roy, a renegade with multiple talents who finds himself dragged in an epic story where every choice counts. Develop your character and your combat style by choosing among many skills and perks: melee, ranged combat, stealth, or the devastating Technomants powers.


Craft armors and weapons, recruit companions to help you in your quest, and plunge in a thrilling adventure offering a huge variety of quests. In dynamic, real-time combat, face formidable opponents and the most fearsome creatures of Mars. The fate of all colonies of Mars now lies in your hands…

reviews.review:
[h1]I found myself up to my neck in the war before I knew it... Before I saw it coming.[/h1]

I heard a lot of praise for this game after playing Greedfall. People were sad that Spiders shut down and they'd miss games like this one and its sequel, so I decided to give it a go, despite the old graphics and clunky controls. 

Years before the events of the game, humans colonized Mars. While water was limited, they were able to build cities and farms, but their only issue was the sun's radiation, which destroyed everything they'd built. Then, two guilds were built to save humanity. Abundance and Aurora, who control how people lived.

You play as Roy, a soldier who is detained and captured by Abundance. One day, new inmates have arrived, and among them is a young boy. After saving the boy from the abusers, you learn his name is Innocence. Everyone from Aurora, including Roy, has a virtue name, but Roy decided to abandon it. The two of them planned to escape the prison, and with a lot of hard work and difficult choices, they were able to leave, and their adventure began. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3827409892

Everything Roy does will influence innocent people, and he'll write it in his journal. Your moral choices will have a huge impact on the story. You could drill your way through everyone by killing them, or leave them be. Roy's reputation does change over time, so you'll have to be careful. The two of them will meet two groups. The government and the resistance, each with their own agenda.  You can only side with one of them, but the story will change drastically, as a single playthrough will not reveal all the information.  

I enjoyed the story a lot, but the gameplay was a little bit clunky. I had a difficult time getting the game to recognize my controller; I had to try a workaround by unplugging my mouse, and it finally worked. The combat was very slow; the animation took a while, and it was usually interrupted by enemies, which was quite annoying, especially the Technomancers' abilities.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3827729286

The soundtracks were good; they capture the post-apocalyptic feel of emptiness and sadness in the areas. The graphics are dated, but I got used to them as the story captured me more than anything. The journal is the best thing in the game; it's called War Logs, just like the title. Innocent will write down every quest you've finished and how he thinks about it. 

The crafting and skills, like all Spider's games, require you to collect items to craft and level up to get skills, which you can mix during the fight. You'll be able to use a makeshift weapon for melee attacks, a needle gun, and a Technomancer fist for magic. And instead of money, you have to collect Serum injections, which can also be used for healing. 

Romance and companions are quite limited; you cannot change their outfits or weapons, and I can't really say they are useful as they die quickly in battle. As for the romance, it seems buggy for one character whom I wanted to be with, so I ended up with another. It is nothing rewarding and doesn't impact the story at all.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3827409989

While the side-quests felt like a chore to go back and forth, and there is no teleportation, finishing them lets you learn more about the lore; how the evil people are not really evil. Everyone is just tired and wants to get back to their family and normal life. Even the guards felt human and understanding; everybody just wants to survive, including the mutants who are doing the hard labor. If Roy decided to help everyone, people would help him back when he needed them.  

Pros:
+Good story.
+Choices have real consequences.
+Switching classes and crafting mid-battle.
+Companions and romance.
+Fitting soundtracks.
+Good voice-overs (Game is fully voiced)
+Multiple endings. (You choose sides)
+Manual save (total of 50, and there are autosaves)
+Cutscenes and dialogues are skippable.
+Steam achievements.

Cons:
-Some backtracking is required. (No fast travelling)
-Clunky controls (both on keyboard and controller)
-Slow combat.

I liked the story a lot, it kept me playing and thinking what would happen next. It is not a bad game, just old and unpolished. Recommended if you enjoy Sci-fi and a post-apocalyptic setting.
